body:
An LLM recognises emotional patterns 94% of the time. Ask it to reason about those emotions and it drops to 67%.

That gap is the paradox I wrote this paper about.

Models have become fluent in the language of emotion. They produce replies that sound caring, fitting and well-timed. But fluency and understanding are different skills, and a reply can sound right while missing what the person actually meant.

In the paper I introduce EmotiScope, a framework that tests both levels separately: surface-level emotional pattern recognition, and deeper emotional reasoning. I ran it across multiple model architectures and cultural contexts, because emotion is not expressed the same way everywhere.

My takeaway for anyone shipping LLMs in customer support, health or education: an empathetic-sounding answer is not evidence of emotional understanding. Measure the reasoning, not the tone.

The full paper is attached below.
